validity.recommendation: Correct StartLocation/EndLocation to Corning, NY -> Ramapo, NY (Rockland County) -- the row's Length (182 mi), Capacity, and StartYear1 (2008) all describe FERC's built 'Phase I Project' under docket CP98-150, not the never-fully-built original 424-mile 2002-approved project whose termini were Lake Erie and Mount Vernon.
validity.researcher_notes: The pipeline is real and operating, but StartLocation='Lake Erie'/EndLocation='Mount Vernon' do not match the specific 182-mile/30-inch/2008 segment the rest of the row describes -- they instead describe an EARLIER, LARGER, never-fully-built version of the same FERC docket. Traced the discrepancy to its root: FERC docket CP98-150 was originally approved 9/19/2002 for ~424 miles running from an interconnect with TransCanada at the US/Canada border in LAKE ERIE (376.4 mi of 36-in pipe) to MOUNT VERNON, NY (39.3 mi of 24-in pipe through Rockland/Westchester Counties) -- confirmed via a Federal Register search returning the FERC order text directly (govinfo.gov FR-2006-01-19/E6-486, which recites the 2002 order's termini and mileage verbatim) plus a Gray & Pape archaeology-firm project page describing the Lake Erie crossing survey for 'the proposed Millennium Pipeline Project.' That 424-mile version was subsequently amended down (petitions at dockets CP98-150-006/-007, noticed 2006-01-19) to a much shorter 'Phase I Project': 'about 181.7 miles of 30-inch-diameter pipeline between milepost (MP) 190.6 to 376.6' running from an interconnection with Empire's system at Corning, NY to the Ramapo Metering & Regulating Station in Rockland County, NY (interconnect with Algonquin) -- this is the segment that was actually built (construction began June 2007, in-service Nov/Dec 2008) and is what the sheet's Length=182, StartYear1=2008 etc. describe. The Corning<->Ramapo routing for THIS built segment is independently confirmed by: Oil & Gas Journal ('186-mile Corning-Ramapo section'/'182-mile' pipeline, 'originates ... Southern Tier ... Corning'), Energy Intelligence ('Connects Empire Connector system at Corning, New York to Algonquin system at Ramapo, New York'), and NiSource's FY2007 10-K SEC filing ('connects Empire pipeline near Corning, NY and extends eastward to interconnect with Algonquin at Ramapo, NY'). GEM's own wiki page (read for leads only, never cited) independently gives a similar-but-not-identical framing ('beginning in Independence, Steuben County to Buena Vista, Rockland County') -- still nowhere near Lake Erie or Mount Vernon. Five sources total (FERC notice + 3 independent secondary + GEM's own wiki text) agree the built pipeline is a Corning-area-to-Ramapo-area line; none place it at Lake Erie or Mount Vernon. StartState/EndState (both already 'New York') are correct and untouched.

validity.recommendation: Correct Diameter to a uniform 30-inch (drop the 14 and 24); correct SegmentCost to ~$654 million (FERC-certified); Capacity is a closer call -- flag the 500 vs 525(.4) MMcf/d gap for a researcher decision rather than force it.
validity.researcher_notes: DIAMETER: the same FERC amendment notice that pins the route (govinfo.gov FR-2006-01-19) states the built Phase I line is 'about 181.7 miles of 30-inch-diameter pipeline' -- a single, uniform diameter, no mix. Oil & Gas Journal ('182-mile ... 30-in.'), Energy Intelligence ('182 miles of 30-inch pipe'), and NiSource's 10-K ('182-mile-long, 30-inch-diameter pipeline') all independently agree: uniform 30-inch. The sheet's '24' most likely bleeds in from the ORIGINAL (never-built-as-such) 2002 project's eastern Rockland/Westchester-to-Mount Vernon leg, which WAS specified at 24-inch per the same FERC record -- i.e. the same location conflation documented in the attribution finding above, carried into the diameter field. '14' has no source anywhere I found (OGJ, Energy Intelligence, NiSource 10-K, DT Midstream, TC Energy, FERC notice, industrialinfo.com) -- it does not correspond to any known Millennium mainline, lateral, or historical-proposal diameter I could locate; flagging it as unconfirmed/likely a data-entry artifact rather than asserting a specific origin. CAPACITY: OGJ literally states 'Phase 1 designed to transport 500 MMcfd of gas' -- a direct match for the sheet's 500.00. But FERC's OWN 2006 amendment notice states the Phase I project's capacity as 'about 525,400 decatherms per day (Dth/d)' (~525 MMcf/d), and NiSource's 10-K independently states 'transport up to 525,400 Dth per day.' That's FERC's certificate figure plus one more independent corroboration vs. OGJ's single, slightly lower figure -- a real but modest (5%) disagreement. Leaving the contested candidate blank rather than forcing 525.4, since OGJ's exact match to the current sheet value is itself real evidence, not noise; a researcher should weigh FERC's certificate (525.4) against OGJ's stated 500 and decide. COST: NiSource's 10-K and the 2006 FERC notice disclose no cost figure; an earlier (2006, pre-construction) industrialinfo.com article citing FERC's initial estimate says 'over $350 million' capital cost -- clearly stale, since costs typically rise through construction. Natural Gas Intelligence's trade-press article on project completion states directly (confirmed by fetching and reading the full article text): 'FERC certified the project at a cost of $654 million.' Nothing found anywhere corroborates the sheet's $800,000,000 figure; recommend $654,000,000 sourced to NGI/FERC's certification, pending a check against the FERC certificate order itself if a researcher wants a fully primary cite.

This project has a genuinely layered proposal history that makes a single ProposalYear ambiguous rather than simply unresearched: the original CP98-150 docket (424-mile Lake Erie-to-Mount Vernon project) traces to a Federal Register notice as early as 1998 (FR-1998-03-04/98-5532) and was FERC-approved 9/19/2002; the much shorter, actually-built 'Phase I' (181.7 mi, Corning-Ramapo -- what the rest of this row describes) was proposed via amendment petitions to the same docket, noticed in the Federal Register 2006-01-19 (govinfo.gov FR-2006-01-19/E6-486) and again 2006-05-16, then approved by FERC in June 2007. Given the Length/Capacity/StartYear on this row all describe the AS-BUILT Phase I project, not the 1998/2002 original, the more internally-consistent ProposalYear would be the Phase I amendment (~2005-2006) rather than 1998 -- but I could not pin an exact single 'this is when Phase I was first proposed' date with two independent sources agreeing on both year and month, so leaving UNRESOLVED rather than force a specific month. A researcher fixing the Location/Diameter conflation above should decide this at the same time, since it turns on the same original-vs-Phase-I distinction.

Searched Oil & Gas Journal, Energy Intelligence, NiSource's 10-K, DT Midstream's and TC Energy's asset pages, and industrialinfo.com's article -- none state MAOP/operating pressure. A second, independent confirmation (e.g. a PHMSA incident/annual report record, or a later FERC compliance filing) is owed but not found in this pass.

Millennium receives gas from multiple, structurally different interconnects -- TransCanada/Dawn Hub Canadian imports and Empire's system at the western (Corning) end, plus Marcellus/Utica shale-gas laterals added over time (e.g. the Valley Lateral to Wawayanda, NY, and Inergy's Stagecoach-storage North Lateral) -- so it is a blended-supply transmission trunk, not a single-source line. Searched Oil & Gas Journal, Energy Intelligence, DT Midstream, TC Energy, and NiSource's 10-K; none assigns a single controlled-vocabulary FuelSource value, and forcing one (e.g. 'Shale gas' alone) would misrepresent the Canadian-import/Dawn-Hub component. Leaving UNRESOLVED for a researcher to apply GEM's FuelSource vocabulary correctly to a multi-source transmission line.

summary: P0216 is real and operating, but has three sourced concerns: an attribution error (Location fields describe the never-fully-built original 424-mile 2002 Lake Erie-to-Mount Vernon project rather than the actual built 182-mile Corning-to-Ramapo 'Phase I' line the rest of the row describes), a spec error (Diameter should be uniform 30-in, not '14, 24, 30'; SegmentCost should be ~$654M per FERC certification, not $800M; Capacity's 500 vs FERC's 525.4 MMcf/d flagged for a judgment call), and an attribution error on ownership (Owner1='Millennium Pipeline' should be DT Midstream 52.5%/TC Energy 47.5%).
